# General Pre-Implementation Checklist: Homepage and Contact Us Popup

**Purpose**: General pre-implementation review of `spec.md`'s requirement quality — completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, and coverage — before proceeding to `/speckit-tasks` and `/speckit-implement`.
**Created**: 2026-09-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined for what happens when a service card or footer link is activated before real destinations exist (no-op, placeholder page, disabled state)? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases] — Resolved: placeholder links are a no-op (FR-017, Edge Cases).
- [x] CHK002 Are requirements defined for how the popup's close control is exposed to assistive technology, beyond the visual "×" glyph? [Gap, Spec §FR-012] — Resolved: FR-021 requires an accessible name.
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements defined for how a contact form validation error is communicated to screen reader users, beyond "the browser prevents submission and indicates which field"? [Gap, Spec §FR-010] — Reviewed: accepted as covered by native HTML validation (FR-010); no spec change.
- [x] CHK004 Is the expected format of the company website field specified (e.g., whether a scheme is required, whether "company.com" without `https://` is valid)? [Gap, Spec §FR-008] — Reviewed: accepted as free text with no format validation, matching the design reference; no spec change.
- [x] CHK005 Does the footer's requirement (FR-006) account for all footer elements implied elsewhere in the design system reference (e.g., social media links), or are they intentionally out of scope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006] — Resolved: FR-006 and User Story 1 Acceptance Scenario 3 now include social media links.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "readable and correctly laid out" (User Story 1, Acceptance Scenario 4) defined with objective criteria beyond "no overlapping or cut-off content"? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 1] — Resolved: Acceptance Scenario 4 now cites the same 320px–1920px range as SC-003.
- [x] CHK007 Is "a typical broadband connection" (SC-005, originally drafted as SC-007) quantified with a specific bandwidth/latency baseline that a measurement could be run against? [Clarity, Spec §SC-005] — Resolved: SC-005 now specifies a simulated fast 4G profile matching standard Lighthouse throttling.
- [x] CHK008 Is "current versions" of Firefox/Edge (FR-019) defined precisely enough (e.g., latest stable release, N-1) to know when a browser build is in or out of scope? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-019] — Resolved: FR-019 now defines "current" as the latest stable release at time of testing.
- [x] CHK009 Is "released within the last 5 years" (FR-020) anchored to a specific reference point (e.g., release date vs. current date at time of testing) rather than left as a floating window? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-020] — Resolved: FR-020 now defines a rolling 5-year window from time of testing.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Are the Success Criteria numbered consistently and sequentially (SC-007 currently appears between SC-003 and SC-004)? [Consistency, Spec §Success Criteria] — Resolved: renumbered into sequential document order (SC-001 through SC-008, after CHK014 also split SC-002 into two criteria).
- [x] CHK011 Is the contact submission entity referred to consistently (e.g., "Contact Request" vs. "request" vs. "inquiry") across User Scenarios, Functional Requirements, and Key Entities? [Consistency] — Resolved: normalized to "Contact Request" throughout (the quoted UI copy "Request received" is locked design-system text and intentionally left as-is).
- [x] CHK012 Do the popup-closing requirements in FR-012 and the Acceptance Scenarios in User Story 2 agree on every way the popup can be closed (×, scrim, "Done")? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012] — Resolved: FR-012 now explicitly enumerates ×, scrim, and "Done".

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK013 Can SC-001 ("without scrolling past the second section") be verified objectively, given that section boundaries aren't defined in scroll/viewport terms? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001] — Resolved: SC-001 now names the Services section explicitly, anchored to FR-001's fixed section order.
- [x] CHK014 Can SC-002's "under 60 seconds" be measured deterministically, given the interval includes human decision and typing time rather than only system behavior? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002] — Resolved: split into SC-002 (60s human-paced UX budget, explicitly allowing headroom for slower motor/reaction time) and new SC-003 (10s system response-time target, separate metric); all later SC/FR numbering shifted accordingly.
- [x] CHK015 Does SC-004 ("without visual defects") define a reviewer-applicable pass/fail threshold, or does it rely on subjective judgment? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004] — Reviewed: accepted as-is; the responsive layout was already heavily reviewed in the Claude Design system, and the named defect types are concrete enough for human review without further test-code investment.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK016 Are requirements defined for exception scenarios beyond native browser field validation (e.g., a syntactically valid but clearly bogus work email or company website value)? [Coverage, Gap] — Reviewed: accepted as out of scope, no additional validation beyond FR-010's native checks; separately, FR-022 added a mobile keyboard-hint convenience for the email field (no validation change).
- [x] CHK017 Are requirements defined for a visitor who, after seeing the confirmation state, wants to submit a second, different request without a full page reload? [Coverage, Gap] — Reviewed: accepted as-is; a second submission isn't expected to be needed, and if a visitor wants one, the existing close-then-reopen path (FR-013) is sufficient with no dedicated shortcut required.
- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for rapid or repeated interaction with the same control (e.g., the submit or "Contact Us" button activated multiple times in quick succession)? [Coverage, Gap] — Resolved: FR-023 requires disabling the submit control on activation (no double-click handler needed) and re-enabling it on every popup open, regardless of whether the popup is remounted or a toggled singleton.
- [x] CHK019 Are requirements defined for the visitor-facing experience if LCP-affecting assets (fonts, hero background) load slowly or fail, beyond the SC-005 target itself? [Coverage, Gap] — Resolved: FR-024 defines a bounded 3s font-load wait with fallback-and-no-later-swap behavior; Assumptions notes the accepted trade-off with SC-005 in a degraded scenario.

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK020 Does the spec define expected behavior at viewport widths exactly at a layout breakpoint boundary, or only at the "very narrow"/"very wide" extremes named in Edge Cases? [Edge Case, Gap] — Reviewed: accepted as-is; already validated across multiple device profiles in Chrome DevTools within the Claude Design reference. FR-014/SC-004's full 320–1920px range is considered sufficient coverage; no spec change.
- [x] CHK021 Is expected behavior specified for a visitor with both a dark-mode OS preference and a forced-colors/high-contrast mode active simultaneously? [Edge Case, Gap] — Reviewed: accepted as out of scope; not required by the constitution's WCAG 2.1 AA principle or addressed by the design system; no spec change.
- [x] CHK022 Does the spec state whether the primary-need selector's grouped option order must be preserved exactly as specified, or whether browser-driven reordering is acceptable? [Edge Case, Gap] — Reviewed: accepted as a non-issue; native `<select>`/`<optgroup>` elements always render in source order, no browser reorders them; no spec change.

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK023 Are accessibility requirements specified beyond keyboard operability and focus visibility (e.g., minimum color contrast ratios, screen reader labeling) traceable to the constitution's WCAG 2.1 AA principle? [Coverage, Gap] — Resolved: FR-025 adds an explicit WCAG 2.1 AA conformance requirement, tracing to the constitution.
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements defined for the visitor's experience if JavaScript fails to load or execute, given User Story 1 expects content to be understandable "without any interaction beyond scrolling"? [Gap, Spec §User Story 1] — Reviewed: accepted as an unstated side effect of the SSG rendering decision (research.md) rather than a formal requirement; no spec change.
- [x] CHK025 Is "operable via keyboard alone" (FR-015) specific enough about the primary-need `<select>` field's expected keyboard behavior, given it can vary by browser? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015] — Resolved: FR-015 now clarifies that native `<select>` keyboard behavior satisfies it, no custom handling required.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK026 Is the assumption that design system content/layout is "final" (Assumptions) validated against the risk that the design system bundle and this spec could diverge over time? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions] — Reviewed: accepted as out of scope for the spec; per user decision, small live-site tweaks are made directly without a spec update, reserving spec changes for a future radical redesign. No spec change.
- [x] CHK027 Is the dependency on browser-native form validation (FR-010) explicitly documented as an assumption, given it determines what "required field" enforcement looks and behaves like to the visitor? [Assumption, Spec §FR-010] — Reviewed: accepted as already stated directly in FR-010's own wording; a separate Assumptions entry would be redundant. No spec change.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK028 Is there a requirement/acceptance-criteria ID scheme cross-referencing each User Story's acceptance scenarios to the FR-xxx/SC-xxx items they correspond to? [Traceability, Gap] — Reviewed: accepted as out of scope; not required by the spec-kit template, and requirements are already grouped thematically near their originating user stories. No spec change.
- [x] CHK029 Does the "Something else" primary-need value (FR-009) carry any distinguishing data expectation, or could its lack of detail conflict with future lead-routing requirements? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009] — Reviewed: accepted as-is, matching the design reference exactly (no free-text detail field); richer lead routing is a future concern. No spec change.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
